research_goal: Implement project management platform functionality in slices without adding dependencies or rewriting native runtime commands.
coding_context: Existing Next.js/React workspace monitor, Node snapshot collector, TypeScript snapshot model, Tauri desktop shell, and static renderer tests.
source_value_provenance: GitHub Desktop and Git docs confirm repository/workspace import is a primary project management flow.
Tauri dialog docs confirm folder selection should remain a native runtime responsibility.
Linear project overview informs the need for status, milestone, and connected document surfaces.
Local tests and components define the existing contracts for snapshot fields and UI markers.
plan_evidence: GitHub Desktop docs and issues support routing clone/open actions to a dedicated workspace host rather than hiding them in project cards.
Git worktree docs support treating Git repository/worktree boundaries as first-class project units.
Tauri dialog docs and discussion support preserving native folder selection as a runtime command boundary.
Local collector tests are the best verification point for project readiness, report bundle, and customer sanitization contracts.
stack_version_constraints: Do not add new package dependencies in this slice.
Keep native Tauri commands as existing workspace host capabilities.
issue_discussion_sources: local user feedback in this thread
issue_discussion_notes: GitHub Desktop issues show clone/open workspace UX can fail or confuse users in environment-specific cases.
Tauri discussion shows folder picker implementation and permission details are platform-sensitive.
User feedback identifies terminal and first-run complexity as a product risk.
Existing tests show terminal drawer, workspace host, and evaluation surfaces are already available and should be reused.
community_signal_notes: No community signal is used as standalone factual proof.
Official docs and local tests are the implementation basis.
language_decision_notes: The requested feature is primarily snapshot shaping, UI organization, and routing.
Existing Tauri workspace commands already cover folder selection, import, clone, and terminal execution surfaces.
Avoiding Rust changes reduces runtime risk while still making the user flow simpler.
architecture_practitioner_sources: Linear project overview pattern for status and milestones
architecture_options: Add more controls to the existing monolithic ProjectManagementPanel.
Split ProjectManagementPanel into smaller feature components while keeping a single route.
Move project management into a separate app immediately.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected feature-component split because it improves maintainability without breaking routing or deployment.
Rejected adding to the monolith because it worsens the exact complexity the user identified.
Rejected a separate app in this slice because project management is now the primary desktop product and existing runtime surfaces should be reused.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Splitting UI components creates more files but keeps each file small and testable.
Snapshot-level readiness avoids duplicating business logic in React components.
Native commands remain reusable but project action routing is now more direct.
code_reference_notes: Feature panels already use data attributes for static and browser verification.
Collector tests can validate customer sanitization and snapshot shape without browser runtime.
MonitorShell already exposes openSection and openTerminalDrawer, so project routing can reuse those callbacks.
folder_structure_options: Keep all project management UI in one feature file.
Move all project management code into a new top-level package.
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected local subcomponent folder because it keeps ownership near the feature route and keeps files under 500 lines.
The folder has copy/helpers plus metric/workflow/portfolio/detail/side panel components.
A new package would add build and ownership overhead without a current reuse need.
folder_semantics_notes: components/features/project-management/ owns project management subcomponents and copy helpers.
scripts/collect-workspace.mjs remains the snapshot source of truth.
lib/snapshot.ts documents the generated data contract.
maintainability_notes: New project-management files are below 500 lines.
The collector remains larger than ideal but helper functions localize the new project state logic.
Future work can split snapshot type declarations and collector modules without changing the UI contract.
findings: Project cards need actionable routing, not only status display.
Native workspace selection and clone should stay in the existing workspace host boundary.
Snapshot-derived readiness reduces duplicated UI heuristics.
Component splitting solves the immediate maintainability issue without destabilizing the entire monitor shell.
options: Keep project management as status-only portfolio.
Implement snapshot-backed project actions and report bundles in the current desktop route.
Rewrite native workspace commands and terminal orchestration before improving the UI.
Extract a separate project management app immediately.
recommendation: Implement snapshot-backed project actions and report bundles in the current desktop route, using existing workspace host and terminal surfaces.
validation_steps: Run workspace monitor collect with best effort.
Run platform desktop test and check.
Run Browser desktop and mobile smoke checks.
Run omission, resource, and evaluation guards.
risks_or_unknowns: Generated snapshot size may change as new history/spec records are added.
Actual remote clone failures still depend on existing native workspace host behavior.
MonitorShell and snapshot type files remain larger than the preferred long-term target.
Per-tool AI adapter installation automation is outside this slice.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Official docs and local source confirm existing workspace host and terminal surfaces are sufficient for this slice.
post_research_answers.best_option: Extend snapshot state, split the project UI, and route actions into existing surfaces.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It directly reduces user complexity and avoids risky runtime rewrites.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: More monolithic UI increases complexity; native command rewrite is unnecessary; separate app extraction is a larger productization step.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Types, collector, ProjectManagementPanel, new subcomponents, CSS, MonitorShell routing, tests, records.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: Full repository creation automation and per-tool setup automation remain later runtime slices.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Run renderer collect/check/test/build, platform test/check, Browser smoke, docs audit, omission/resource/evaluation guards.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: This record defines project management as snapshot-backed UI plus existing runtime surface routing.
post_research_answers.next_action: Complete generated snapshot, full build, Browser smoke, close-out guards, commit, and push.
